text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Nintendo 64 was released in 1996 as Nintendo's fifth-generation home console and was one of the first systems designed around 3D gameplay. It used cartridge media and introduced the Nintendo 64 controller with an analog stick designed for three-dimensional movement. The system's library included landmark games such as Super Mario 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, GoldenEye 007, Mario Kart 64, Super Smash Bros., Star Fox 64, and Banjo-Kazooie. The console supported four-player gaming without requiring additional adapters and featured accessories such as the Rumble Pak and Expansion Pak. Although cartridge limitations affected some third-party support, the Nintendo 64 played a major role in the transition from 2D to 3D console gaming.
